Rarity.rationale: Obtainable: not in the grab bag (Event rarity), granted by the ported Colossal Flower event -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b12.py b12-pool` reports granted_by=['sts2_rl/events/colossal_flower.py'], matching the port's docstring. Event rarity also makes it untradable via Relic.is_tradable (relics/base.py:134-136), matching RelicModel.IsTradable.

ShowCounter.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / base.Status / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / UpdateDisplay / CanonicalVars / Cmd.Wait are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow and counter. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.

DisplayAmount.rationale: PollinousCore.cs:29-39 shows TurnsSeen, or the Turns var while the activation animation runs. Same presentation exclusion as ShowCounter.

BeforeSideTurnStart.rationale: PollinousCore.cs:90-98 increments TurnsSeen for the owner's side turn, and the only thing that must hold is that it runs before ModifyHandDraw reads the counter. It does on both sides: audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json orders BeforeSideTurnStart -> ... -> ModifyHandDraw -> Draw, and the sim's executed order (`py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order`) is on_block_cleared -> on_energy_reset -> on_player_turn_start -> modify_hand_draw -> on_player_turn_started -- so on_player_turn_start is the pre-draw slot and the mapping is executed, not read off relics/base.py's docstring (PROMPT.md bug class 11). EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b12.py b12-pollinous): turns_seen reads 1,2,3,0,1,2 across six turns and the 7-card hand lands on turn 4. `participants.Contains(base.Owner.Creature)` is the player-side filter and `player is self.player` (pollinous_core.py:28) is its single-player form. NOTE per binding rule 7: turn_structure.json, relic_probes.py, hooks.py and relics/base.py are not hashed here.

AfterCombatEnd.maps_to: no counterpart -- and none is needed
AfterCombatEnd.rationale: PollinousCore.cs:100-104 assigns `base.Status = RelicStatus.Normal` and NOTHING else; it does not touch TurnsSeen. Same presentation exclusion as ShowCounter; see guard N1 for why the missing counter reset is correct.

ModifyHandDraw.maps_to: modify_hand_draw (pollinous_core.py:31-35), dispatched by HookSystem.modify_hand_draw (hooks.py:217-222) from PlayerCombatState.start_turn (player.py:171)
ModifyHandDraw.rationale: Rollup of guard G1 per binding rule 4. The test and the amount are exact -- `TurnsSeen != Turns` -> unchanged, else `count + Cards.BaseValue` (PollinousCore.cs:106-117) vs `self.turns_seen != self.TURNS` -> unchanged, else `count + self.CARDS` (pollinous_core.py:32-35), with TURNS = 4 and CARDS = 2 (guard N2). Note both sides use an exact `!=` rather than `>=`, so the relic is equally fragile on both sides if the counter ever overshoots. The divergence is that the sim performs the RESET inside this modifier where C# performs it in the separate AfterModifyingHandDraw event -- guard G1, same observable.

AfterModifyingHandDraw.maps_to: folded into modify_hand_draw (pollinous_core.py:34, `self.turns_seen = 0`) -- the sim has no after_modifying_hand_draw hook at all
AfterModifyingHandDraw.rationale: See guard G1. PollinousCore.cs:119-124 resets TurnsSeen to 0 and fires the activation animation; the sim does the reset one hook earlier, inside the modifier itself, under the identical condition. The animation half is presentation (see ShowCounter). This is the one port in the pool that actually NEEDS the missing hook, which is worth recording against relic/bag_of_preparation N1 and audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json step 20, where the hook's absence is verdicted as a dormant gap on the machinery: at this site it is not dormant, it is worked around. NOTE per binding rule 7: bag_of_preparation.json and turn_structure.json are not hashed here.

guards.what: G1: the sim mutates state inside a MODIFIER hook (modify_hand_draw) where C# mutates it in the following EVENT hook (AfterModifyingHandDraw) -- and the two are equivalent, because C# dispatches AfterModifyingHandDraw only to listeners that actually changed the count
guards.rationale: This is the entry that had to be settled by reading the DISPATCHER rather than the relic. Hook.ModifyHandDraw (src/Core/Hooks/Hook.cs:1684-1696) folds every listener's ModifyHandDraw and collects into `list` only those for which `(int)num2 != (int)num` -- i.e. only the listeners whose call changed the integer count. Hook.AfterModifyingHandDraw (Hook.cs:739-749) then walks the listeners and calls the method ONLY `if (modifiers.Contains(modifier))`. So C#'s `TurnsSeen = 0` fires exactly on the turns the bonus was granted, which is precisely the condition pollinous_core.py:32-34 puts the reset behind. Had the dispatch been unconditional, the C# relic would reset every turn and never reach 4 at all -- the reading that makes this look like a gap is the one that makes the source's own relic non-functional, which is the tell. There is one residual difference: a modifier hook is supposed to be a pure read, and the sim's is not, so any caller that consults modify_hand_draw twice per turn would consume the bonus on the first call. There is exactly one caller (player.py:171) and it is called once per player turn, so the observable is identical today. Recorded as a divergence rather than faithful for that reason, and flagged for whoever adds a hand-draw PREVIEW: previews.py already does this for damage, block and cost, and a hand-draw preview would silently break this relic. EXECUTED (b12-pollinous): the bonus lands on turn 4 and only turn 4, the counter returns to 0 there, and the cycle repeats from turn 5. NOTE per binding rule 7: Hook.cs, hooks.py, player.py and previews.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N1 (the sweep-A candidate, settled): `turns_seen` carries into combat 2 and that is INTENDED ON BOTH SIDES
guards.rationale: `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py sweep-reset` lists pollinous_core with `C# resets: {'AfterCombatEnd': ['base.Status = RelicStatus.Normal']}` and sweep-reset-exec puts it among the 12 candidates that agree with a fresh instance; the sweeps doc names it a sweep-A candidate to settle by execution. Settled: TurnsSeen is a [SavedProperty] (PollinousCore.cs:61-74) so it survives a save/load, and the sole statement in the C# AfterCombatEnd body is the display-flag assignment (PollinousCore.cs:102). 'Every 4 player turns' is a run-level count on both sides, and the sim's relic instance living on RunState.relics and being re-attached to every CombatState (run.py:1153) is exactly the persistence it needs -- which the port's own docstring states correctly (pollinous_core.py:10-13), unlike relic/pendulum's in this batch. PROMPT.md bug class 13's reader-trace: the reader is modify_hand_draw, and a run-level counter is what it is meant to see. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b12.py b12-pollinous): leaving combat 1 with turns_seen = 3 makes combat 2's FIRST turn the one that draws 7, where a fresh instance draws 5 -- the carry changes which turn pays out, exactly as the [SavedProperty] does in the game. Same family and same verdict as relic/happy_flower N1, relic/fake_happy_flower N1 and relic/pendulum N1 (binding rule 3). NOTE per binding rule 7: relic_probes.py, content-relic-sweeps.md, run.py, pendulum.json, happy_flower.json and fake_happy_flower.json are not hashed here.

guards.what: N2: `CardsVar(2)` and `DynamicVar('Turns', 4m)` (PollinousCore.cs:41-45), read as Cards.BaseValue and Turns.IntValue vs TURNS = 4 and CARDS = 2 (pollinous_core.py:20-21)
guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file, so 4 and 2 are the pinned non-ascension values. The port annotates each constant with the C# expression it comes from, which is exactly the pattern PROMPT.md bug class 19 warns can protect a WRONG number -- so both were re-read against the source: CardsVar(2) and DynamicVar('Turns', 4m) confirmed, and confirmed again by the executed cycle in b12-pollinous (bonus on turn 4, hand 5 -> 7).

guards.what: N3: `TurnsSeen++` is unbounded in C# (PollinousCore.cs:96) and `+= 1` is unbounded in the sim (pollinous_core.py:29) -- neither takes a modulo, so both rely on the reset firing to keep the `!= Turns` test reachable
guards.rationale: Contrast relic/pendulum, whose counter wraps with `% Turns` on both sides. Here the only thing that returns the counter to 0 is the bonus itself, so a turn on which ModifyHandDraw is not dispatched at all would push the counter past 4 and disable the relic permanently -- identically on both sides, since neither has a fallback. Recorded because it means the port must NOT be 'improved' to `>=` without the game doing the same, and because it is the reason the reset's condition (guard G1) is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. No such skipped dispatch exists today: player.py:171 calls modify_hand_draw on every player turn start.

Presentation, same exclusion as ShowCounter. Fired with RunSafely and not awaited, so its `await Cmd.Wait(1f)` cannot delay anything -- the same finding relic/fake_happy_flower N4 recorded for the identical idiom.
